transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess the short version is that I’m not functioning the way I usually do. My in-laws moved into our house, and since then I’ve just been… constantly keyed up, like I can’t ever fully relax in my own home. And at the same time I’m worn down, like I’m running on fumes.

It’s spilling into everything. I’ve been snapping at my wife over things I normally wouldn’t, and then I feel terrible about it, but in the moment I just react. Work has been affected too, which is really why I finally thought, okay, I need to talk to someone. I manage artists—musicians, performers—and I’m usually very on top of calls, contracts, details, all of it. But lately I’ve been avoiding calls I would normally handle right away, just letting them sit because I can’t deal with one more conversation. And I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart because I couldn’t think straight enough to keep all the pieces moving.

That’s not like me. I’m used to pressure, honestly, but this feels different. It’s like I’m overloaded all the time.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with family and friends?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I don’t think it’s like I suddenly don’t care about the things I usually like, if that’s what you mean. It’s more that everything feels harder to get to, or I don’t have the same room in my head for it.

Like, with work, I still care a lot—probably too much, honestly—but I’m not enjoying it the way I usually do because I’m so preoccupied and tense. And with people, I haven’t really been thinking, “I don’t want to see anyone ever again,” it’s more like… I’m tired before anything even starts, so I don’t initiate as much. But I don’t know if that counts as losing interest or just being overwhelmed.
Have you found yourself worrying a lot more than usual, even about things that wouldn’t typically bother you, and does it feel hard to stop worrying once you start?

Yeah… I mean, I think “worrying” is part of it, but it feels bigger than just worry. Since my in-laws moved into the house, it’s like my baseline is just… keyed up. I’m always bracing for something, even when nothing is actually happening right that second.

And once I get going in my head, it’s hard to shut it off. I’ll start thinking about one thing—like a call I need to return, or something at home—and then it turns into everything at once. I’m worn down from it. That’s when I end up snapping at my wife over something small, or avoiding calls I’d normally handle immediately because I just can’t face one more thing. And at work, that’s really scared me, because I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart just because I couldn’t think clearly enough to keep track of what needed to happen.

So yes, I’d say it’s much more than usual, and it’s hard to stop once it starts.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like restlessness, trouble sleeping, muscle tension, or trouble concentrating along with feeling keyed up and overwhelmed?

Yeah… I mean, the biggest physical-feeling part is that keyed-up feeling. It’s like my body and my head are both on alert all the time since my in-laws moved into the house. I feel worn down, like I don’t have any margin left.

And it’s definitely affecting my concentration. That’s actually one of the things that scared me into coming in. I’m usually very organized with work—calls, contracts, keeping track of artists and what needs to happen next—but lately I’ve been avoiding calls I’d normally return right away, just because I feel like I can’t take in one more thing. And I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart because I just couldn’t think straight and keep the pieces together.

At home it comes out too. I’ll be so tense and overloaded that I snap at my wife over something small, and then afterward I’m sitting there thinking, “Why did I react like that?” So… yes, I’m feeling it in my body as being constantly keyed up, and in my head as being worn down and not able to concentrate the way I normally can.
Have you felt like you’re not enjoying things that you used to take pleasure in, even when you’re not stressed or overwhelmed?

I’m not sure I can separate it that cleanly, honestly. Like, if you’re asking whether I’m sitting there on a perfectly calm day, with nothing pressing on me, and realizing I don’t enjoy music or dinner with friends or time with my wife anymore… I don’t know that I’d say that.

It feels more like there hasn’t been much of a version of me that isn’t stressed or overwhelmed lately, so it’s hard to test the question, if that makes sense. I still think I would enjoy those things if I could actually settle into them. I don’t feel like pleasure is gone exactly. It’s more like it’s hard to access because my mind is already crowded before I even get there.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed a clear “I don’t enjoy anything anymore” feeling when I’m otherwise okay. I’m just not sure I’ve had many moments lately where I’m otherwise okay enough to tell.
Have you noticed feeling anxious or worried even when there isn’t a specific problem or stressor on your mind at that moment?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not always tied to a specific thing I can point to, like, “Oh, I’m worried about this one bill,” or “I’m worried about this one meeting.” A lot of the time it’s more like I’m already on edge before my brain has even picked a reason.

Since my in-laws moved into the house, I feel like I’m carrying this constant pressure around. Even if nothing is happening in that exact moment, I’m still kind of bracing myself. And then it spills into everything. I snap at my wife over things that, if I were calmer, probably wouldn’t even register. I avoid calls I would normally just handle right away because I feel too overloaded to deal with one more conversation. And at work, that really scared me—I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart because I couldn’t think straight.

So yes, I guess the answer is yes. Sometimes there’s a clear stressor, but sometimes it’s just this background feeling of being keyed up and worn down, even before I know what I’m supposedly worried about.
Have you found yourself feeling down, sad, or hopeless most of the day, more days than not, even before the in-laws moved in?

No… not before they moved in. I mean, I had normal stress, like anyone does—work can be a lot, and I’ve had busy stretches—but I was functioning normally. I wasn’t walking around feeling down or hopeless most of the day or anything like that.

This really feels like it started after my in-laws moved into the house and, honestly, kind of took over the space. Within a few weeks, I could feel myself changing. Before that, I was handling my life. I was doing my job, keeping up with things, feeling like myself. Then once the house stopped feeling like my own and that pressure built up, that’s when everything started to go sideways.

So if you’re asking whether this was already there before them—no. I don’t think so. It feels tied to that change pretty clearly.
